title: Expressing Detriment with rovására ('at the expense of / to the detriment of')

sections.title: Grammatical Formation and Structure
sections.content: The compound postposition rovására (historically 'onto its notch/tally-stick') functions as an analytical postposition meaning 'at the expense of' or 'to the detriment of'. The preceding noun appears either in the unmarked nominative or with a possessive suffix: a minőség rovására ('at the expense of quality'), a közösség rovására ('to the detriment of the community').

sections.title: Socioeconomic and Analytical Contexts
sections.content: In formal Hungarian discourse, rovására expresses asymmetrical trade-offs where gain in one sphere directly inflicts damage or sacrifice on another: 'A mennyiségi termelés növelése a talaj termőképességének rovására történt' ('Increasing quantitative output occurred at the expense of soil fertility').

sections.title: Examples of rovására in Socioeconomic Prose
rows: A gazdasági növekedés nem mehet a természet rovására.
Economic growth cannot come at the expense of nature.
A tanyai önellátás az iskoláztatás rovására valósult meg.
Farmstead self-sufficiency was achieved at the expense of schooling.
A gyors iparosítás a mezőgazdaság rovására történt.
Rapid industrialization occurred at the expense of agriculture.
A munkahelyi hajsza a családi élet rovására ment.
The workplace rat race came at the expense of family life.

items.spanish: A tanyák anyagi biztonsága sokszor a gyermekek tanulásának rovására valósult meg.
items.english: The material security of the homesteads was often realized at the expense of children's education.

items.spanish: A szocialista nehézipar erőltetett fejlesztése a fogyasztási cikkek rovására történt.
items.english: The forced development of socialist heavy industry happened at the expense of consumer goods.

items.spanish: Nem szabad a gyors nyereséget a fenntarthatóság rovására hajszolni.
items.english: One must not chase quick profit at the expense of sustainability.

sections.title: B2 Usage Notice
sections.content: Use rovására whenever a decision or historical process creates an unintended victim or measurable sacrifice!
